subject: Security exhibit Q&A + pen-test window for order form
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@brightlinehealth.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: initial order form + security exhibit questions

Thanks Avery — we reviewed the draft order form and security exhibit. A couple of quick clarifying asks before we hand to procurement: 1) the pen-test language refers to 'reasonable notice' — can you confirm the minimum notice window (Brightline is asking for 30 days, is that acceptable?), 2) we need a short list of what evidence artifacts Redwood can provide live (log extracts, SOC 2 report links, ephemeral staging access), and 3) how does Redwood propose handling remediation timelines for high/critical findings discovered during the agreed window?

Attachments: Brightline_Redlines_v1.pdf (pdf, 82KB)

Regards,
Maya Singh
Director, Security & Compliance
Brightline Health

From: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
To: Maya Singh <maya@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-16T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: initial order form + security exhibit questions

Maya — thanks, great questions. Quick answers and proposed path: 

- Pen-test notice: Redwood prefers 14 business days as our standard; we can accept 30 calendar days if Brightline requires it for vendor scheduling. We suggest documenting "no less than 14 business days" in the exhibit and allowing mutual agreement to extend.

- Evidence artifacts: we can provide a SOC 2 Type II report (scoped controls and auditor statement), a redacted system architecture diagram, scoped KV cache access logs for the staging window, and a CSV evidence export mapping (sample attached). We cannot provide full raw production logs or PII extracts; access will be scoped to a dedicated ephemeral staging environment for the pen-test.

- Remediation timeline: proposed SLA is triage within 48 hours for Critical, mitigation plan within 10 business days, and documented closure within 30 calendar days. For Critical issues that affect customer data flows we commit to immediate mitigation/fallback and an incident timeline. We can add a short remediation table in the exhibit.

I've attached a working evidence mapping template (evidence-mapping-template.csv) and a redline of the security exhibit with inline suggestions. Karthik / Laura / Soojin — can you weigh in on whether the 14 business day default + 30 calendar day opt-in looks good from legal/ops?

Thanks — Avery
Avery Johnson
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-17T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: initial order form + security exhibit questions

Avery — flagged a few drafting notes for the security exhibit redline: 

1) "Reasonable notice" needs a numeric floor or we'll repeatedly get asked to extend. I support 14 business days as a sensible default; add language for mutual written agreement to extend to 30 calendar days for scheduled enterprise tests.

2) Pen-test scope: avoid blanket "production access" wording. We should state testers get access to an ephemeral staging tenancy with representative sample data; permit read-only access to KV cache logs and request-response traces stripped of PII.

3) Evidence retention: Brightline asked for evidence exports — propose we commit to making artifacts available for 30 days post-test (download window) and retain internal telemetry for 90 days for incident follow-up. Do not promise longer-term retention without product/legal approval.

4) Remediation: tighten the SLA table to specify severity definitions (Critical/High/Medium/Low) with concrete timeboxes; do not commit to code changes within 10 business days for anything beyond 'mitigation plan' acceptance.

I'll mark these in the redline (see Brightline_OrderForm_Redlines_v3.pdf) and propose the following next step: a short 30-minute ops + security call with Brightline to walk scope and confirm the ephemeral environment capabilities before we finalize the exhibit.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Maya Singh <maya@brightlinehealth.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, paul.reed@brightlinehealth.com
Date: 2027-06-18T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: initial order form + security exhibit questions

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the templates — this is helpful. A few points from our side after internal check: 

- 30-day calendar notice is preferred for planning (procurement + external testers). If Redwood will accept 14 business days as baseline and allow Brightline to opt for 30 calendar days, that is acceptable.

- Ephemeral staging with representative data works, provided Redwood documents the exact endpoints available and confirms that KV traces will be redacted of PII prior to export. We will need an export sample (sanitized) during the ops call.

- Evidence availability for 30 days post-test is fine. For longer forensic needs Brightline will request a scoped extension and we understand Redwood may need additional approvals/costs for that.

Next step: Paul (cc'd) will send two proposed windows for an ops call next week. Please include the engineering lead who can validate endpoint and log access (So if Soojin can join that call, great).

Regards,
Maya
Director, Security & Compliance, Brightline Health
